content:
[L] high | Audit trail table | The "AI" column is crushed against the table's right border and its values ("ai" pill, "—") nearly touch the edge, with the table extending to the window edge with no margin.
[S] med | Audit trail table, "AI" column | Column widths are wildly uneven — ACTOR and CONVERSATION columns occupy large widths for trivial content while the AI column is starved, breaking any sensible grid.
[S] med | Event log rows | Vertical gaps between the three log rows are uneven (row spacing visibly larger between rows 2 and 3 than between 1 and 2).
[S] med | Bottom of window | Large empty dead zone below the audit trail detail line while the event log panel above is also mostly empty — the fixed panel heights waste most of the vertical space.
[H] med | Event log, JSON detail line | The raw payload `{"kind":"create_reply"}` floats orphaned under the log row with no container or label, reading as debug output rather than product UI.
[H] med | Audit trail footer | The detail line `#1 before: "active" after: "pending"` is unanchored raw debug text floating below the table with no heading or pairing to its row.
[H] low | Tab row vs "Event log" heading | Filter chips (All 3 / Errors 1 / Warnings 1 / Info 1) carry heavier visual weight (dark filled chip) than the panel heading, inverting heading/label hierarchy.
[H] low | Table column headers | ALL-CAPS headers (WHEN, ACTOR, ACTION, CONVERSATION) are the only caps in the UI, competing with the pill-style tags which use lowercase.
[C] med | Whole screen | Only 3 log events and 2 audit rows fill a full desktop window at maybe 15% content density; the screen reads as a sparse debug view, not a product.
[C] low | Audit trail detail area | The `#1 before/after` line implies per-row detail but is detached from its row, creating an ungrouped floating element.
[S] low | Header area | Description sentence runs nearly edge-to-edge with tighter inset than the panel below, so header and panel content do not share a left margin grid.

VERDICT: needs-work — the structure is recognizable as a product, but crushed columns, orphaned debug payloads, and vast empty regions keep it well below professional standards.
